summary: Reviewed e74b152a0cc216daaf7f1c51fcaea89761f84b11..2b219573fcbdf1fb03b0ec3f53889036d4274636 for #1324. The five original defect groups and subsequent ignored-output/cache/root repairs are supported by source and recorded evidence. One P2 regression remains: a returned file-to-directory replacement deletes the unchanged local parent file but rejects its new child before that deletion is applied. This is a source prediction, not a newly executed reproducer. Recorded final evidence reports 15 passing tests at evidence/codex-review-audit/exec-writeback-root-final.txt:93 and exit 0 at line 97; those fixtures do not cover this transition. All 21 changed Rust files and both inspected gateway files match the latest applicable recorded SHA-256 manifests. No repository tests, builds, lint, formatting, source edits, publication or delegation were performed during this review.

findings.title: Apply new children when an unchanged parent file is replaced by a directory
findings.detail: Start with an ordinary existing artifacts/report.txt on the client and node, and make no concurrent local edits. A remote command removes that file and creates artifacts/report.txt/part.txt instead. The real gateway returns the parent deletion followed by the new child. Writeback queues the accepted parent deletion, but it validates every delta against the still-unchanged local filesystem before applying that queue. Reading the child through the existing regular-file parent produces NotADirectory, which this branch labels as a local conflict. The subsequent apply deletes the parent and never writes the child, while both public runners can still return the successful remote exit. Thus ordinary remote deletion/new-output writeback loses the replacement output. This behavior is introduced by the aggregate's new error-to-kept branch; it is not a request to redesign pre-existing sync behavior.
findings.evidence: Source prediction only; no new test or filesystem probe was run. Semantic terminal command prod-code def --symbol Writeback::apply returned the definition at crates/prod-code-mcp/src/exec/writeback.rs:176 and the error-to-kept branch at lines 194-196, exit 0. FileState::read_limited recognizes only NotFound as absence at crates/prod-code-mcp/src/exec/writeback.rs:35-38, so an intermediate regular file produces an error. The accepted deltas are not applied until line 226. Real gateway reachability: crates/prod-code-gateway/src/seed_cache/build_cache.rs:220-230 traverses the resulting directory and emits its child; crates/prod-code-gateway/src/runner/snapshot.rs:291-309 emits new content, lines 312-319 emit the old parent deletion, and line 321 sorts parent before child. The unchanged writer at crates/prod-code-mcp/src/sync/pull.rs:40-61 can apply this ordered deletion then creation. At aggregate base e74b152a0cc216daaf7f1c51fcaea89761f84b11, git show confirmed crates/prod-code-mcp/src/exec/runner.rs:75-92 converted the child's read failure to absence and queued both deltas, so the parent deletion allowed the subsequent child write. Both current public runners invoke the same Writeback::apply at crates/prod-code-mcp/src/exec/runner.rs:69 and :155. The recorded final suite's new-path fixtures use already-directory or absent parents (crates/prod-code-mcp/tests/exec_writeback_preservation/directories.rs:35-41 and roots.rs:54-59), so their success does not refute this filesystem barrier.
findings.suggested_fix: Handle an accepted parent-file deletion and its returned child creations coherently within the batch. Recognize absence caused by an unchanged ancestor that this same batch has validated for deletion, retain refusal for actual local edits/deletions and unknown symlink paths, and refresh the deleted-file identity without trying to read the replacement directory as a regular file. Preserve ordinary writeback rather than refusing the whole batch.
